# Track

Track is a small open-source task board for one person and their AI agents.
One Go binary, standard library only, MIT license. Each card is a markdown
file in a git repo. Agents use the track command; people use a Linear-style
web page served on 127.0.0.1:4747.

Source and README: https://github.com/FatherMarz/track

## Install

go install github.com/FatherMarz/track@latest
track init ~/track-data     # the data repo, separate from the program

## Core commands

track add <project> "<title>" [--priority p] [--label l] [--due YYYY-MM-DD] [--as agent]
track capture "<spoken words>"   # finds the project in the words
track list [--project p] [--status s] [--filter "..."] [--all] [--json]
track show <ID> [--json]
track move <ID> <status>          # backlog, todo, in-progress, in-review, done, canceled
track edit <ID> [flags]
track note <ID> "<text>"
track check                       # card files Track cannot read
track sync                        # push the data repo to its remote
track serve                       # the web board

## Facts

- Free, open source, MIT. No account, no cloud, no telemetry, no database.
- Code and data are separate repos. The program holds nothing about your work.
- Every change is a git commit that names who made it (me or agent).
- Hand edits to card files are committed automatically; unreadable cards are flagged, never dropped.
- The web page has a command menu (Cmd+K), saved views, arrow-key movement and a phone layout.
- Agents must change cards with the track command, not by editing files.
